items.note: Matches ESC 2021 diuretic algorithm: 1x oral dose given, urine Na 38 and ~70 mL/h, warm and wet, so doubling the loop dose is the only best answer; distractors each right elsewhere.
Persistent community S. aureus bacteraemia, new murmur, negative TTE: TOE is ESC 2023 class I and the single best answer; realistic stem, cloxacillin fits region.
Key D fits ESC 2023 high-risk tier and stem excludes very-high-risk; but <24 h is only class IIa now, so inpatient angiography by 72 h is not indefensible in practice.
Coherent, realistic new AF with HF; echo, flat troponin, TSH fit; key right on CHA2DS2-VA 4, apixaban 5 mg, no non-DHP CCB at EF<=40%, 24-h cardioversion rule. JVP 4 cm a touch low.

feedback.note: All three explanations accurate and correctly attributed to ESC 2021/2023; class IIa downgrade and TIMACS/VERDICT right; honest about which sources were not re-opened.
Claims accurate (RACE II, EAST-AFNET 4, 24-h rule, dose rule; checked EHRA). Flaws: EHRA interval misquoted as six-monthly (it is 4), half mark harsh, EAST CI is 96% not 95%.
Re-read EHRA 2021 (I checked: 4-monthly at 75+, CrCl/10 confirmed), conceded ungraded status, corrected its own misquote, restored the mark and kept the teaching point.

quality.note: Accurate, current ESC-based round well pitched for an internist; only blemishes a misquoted EHRA interval and a harsh half mark, both corrected on challenge, and the IIa softness of Q3.
concerns: Final feedback as sent says EHRA advises about six-monthly renal checks at 75+; EHRA 2021 says 4-monthly (corrected only in the dispute reply).
round.json still carries the withdrawn minor knowledge error and a key-learning line saying 'every 4-6 months', with grade_changes empty; check the dispute outcome reached the record.
Q3: with the <24 h target now class IIa in ESC 2023, option B (within 72 h) is partly defensible; consider rewording B or the question to 'guideline-recommended target'.
Final feedback quotes the EAST-AFNET 4 interval as 95% CI; the trial reported a 96% CI (0.66-0.94). From memory, not re-checked online.
Final feedback gave mastery 5/5 alongside a half mark and a coded knowledge error for the same item; internally inconsistent before the dispute.
Case exam gives JVP 4 cm above the sternal angle, which is borderline rather than clearly raised; fits 'mild' failure but a higher value would be cleaner.
